jess_customer: Hey @maria_support — we started seeing a spike of 429 + AbortError in our Node service after updating to ts-sdk@1.3.0. Requests to /v1/generate get retried and then the fetch throws 'The user aborted a request'.

maria_support: Thanks Jess. Can you paste a minimal repro or the snippet you're using to call the SDK? Also which Node version and undici (if you're pinning) please.

jess_customer: Node 18.16.0, not pinning undici explicitly. Using the official TS client like: ````
const res = await client.responses.create({ model: 'redwood/small', input: 'hi' });
````

maria_support: Got it. When you say spike after updating to 1.3.0 — was 1.2.x working fine? Any proxy or network middleware that might add timeouts?

jess_customer: Yes 1.2.4 was fine. No proxy timeouts. We see the following pattern in logs: "request attempt 1 -> 429 -> retry -> attempt 2 -> abort". Full error: "FetchError: The user aborted a request".

matt_eng: Jumping in — this smells like an interaction between the SDK retry wrapper and AbortController lifecycle. In some older retry implementations we reused the same AbortSignal across attempts which can get aborted on a later attempt and leak back to in-flight fetch.

zoe_devex: Can you share the SDK config you pass? e.g. any custom retry/backoff? The TS SDK allows options like `retry.maxRetries` and `retry.backoff` or a custom `signal`.

jess_customer: We only set maxRetries: 2 and left default backoff. Example config: ````
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, retry: { maxRetries: 2 } });
````

matt_eng: Ok. Two quick repros to try: 1) pin undici to 5.x (if using native fetch polyfill) or upgrade undici if pinned; 2) try setting retry.backoff to a simple exponential instead of jitter to see if timing hides it. But the real fix is in how the SDK constructs AbortControllers across retry attempts. We returned the same signal sometimes — that leads to a later abort to affect previous promise.

maria_support: @matt_eng any quick patch/workaround we can suggest to customer right now?

matt_eng: Workaround: create your own AbortController per request and pass its signal into the SDK call (SDK will not reuse it across retries). Example: ````
const ac = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 15000); // optional timeout
await client.responses.create({ model: 'redwood/small', input: 'hi', signal: ac.signal });
````

jess_customer: Trying that now... also I can reproduce locally by mocking a 429 on first attempt and a delayed 200 on second. With custom signal it stopped throwing aborts but we still get a retry failure occasionally.

zoe_devex: Another quick check: run `node --version` and `npm ls undici` to see if another dependency pulls a different undici. Duplicate undici versions can cause mixed fetch behavior.

jess_customer: Ran `npm ls undici` — nothing, so runtime uses global fetch.

matt_eng: Thanks. I'm going to open a patch to ensure the SDK creates a fresh internal AbortController per attempt unless the user passes their own signal. That will prevent the leaked aborts. In the meantime, two options: 1) pass your own AbortController (as above), or 2) downgrade to ts-sdk@1.2.4 which didn't have the bug.

maria_support: I'll escalate to eng and link this thread. @matt_eng can you add a short repro snippet in the issue so support can reference it?

matt_eng: Yep — creating issue RW-2321 with repro and a unit test that simulates 429 + delayed success. Patch will target 1.3.x -> 1.3.1.

jess_customer: Thanks. We'll pin to 1.2.4 for now and try the AbortController workaround in staging. Appreciate the fast help. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deployed patch branch matt/retry-abort-fix -> staging at 2026-03-04T14:12:00Z (will run integration tests).

zoe_devex: Follow-ups for docs: call out that if you pass a custom `signal` it should be per-request and that the SDK will not reuse it (until patch). Also note recommended backoff strategy: jittered exponential helps avoid thundering herd on 429s.

matt_eng: PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/r/repo/pulls/451 — test + changelog included.

jess_customer: Confirmed workaround works in staging. Will re-open here if anything pops. Thanks all!"
